topics.title: Add collectible power-ups: Double Points, Slow-Mo, and Shrink
topics.trigger: The game needed a new gameplay hook beyond ordinary food, giving players occasional temporary boosts or twists during a run.
topics.response:
- Added a new power-up collectible system in the main game engine: after eating food there's a chance a Double Points, Slow-Mo, or Shrink pickup spawns on the board, lingers for a limited number of moves, and visibly blinks as it nears expiry.
- Double Points doubles score gains for a set duration, Slow-Mo stretches the game's tick speed for a duration (affecting the shared clock even in two-snake bot matches), and Shrink instantly trims several tail segments off the collecting snake.
- Added HUD elements (a status badge showing the active effect and countdown, and a pop-up toast naming the pickup just collected) plus color-coded visuals per power-up type, and a URL override (`?powerup=type` or `off`) to force deterministic spawns for testing.
topics.decisions:
- **Excluded from human two-player mode**: Power-ups only appear in single-player and bot-vs-bot modes, since a shared power-up in human two-player would create ambiguity over which player's pickup effect applies.
- **Per-snake effects, shared clock for Slow-Mo**: Double Points and Shrink apply only to the snake that grabbed them, but Slow-Mo slows the single shared game loop whenever either snake holds it, since there's only one tick timer driving the board.
- **Deterministic test override**: A URL parameter forces a specific power-up type to spawn directly in the snake's path, making the feature reliably testable without waiting on random spawn odds.

topics.title: Teach all snake bots to react to power-ups without losing their personality
topics.trigger: Once power-ups existed on the board, the automated bots needed to notice and optionally pursue them, but each bot has a distinct movement style that shouldn't be flattened into all bots simply beelining for the nearest pickup.
topics.response:
- Built a shared power-up scoring helper module that every bot calls with one added line, using a per-bot "appetite" configuration (overall pursuit strength, per-type bonus multipliers, and an optional gating rule) so each bot's existing scoring logic stays intact.
- Extended the shared bot data types and the position-analysis routine (in the main game and the menu demo) to compute the shortest path from a candidate move to the power-up, so pursuit decisions account for reachability and how long the pickup will remain on the board.
- Tuned all twelve bots individually: e.g. the aggressive Chaser bot favors Double Points and Slow-Mo, the tightly-coiling bot strongly favors Shrink, the ambush bot only strikes for pickups within its lurking range, the survival-focused bot never diverts if doing so would strand it, and the perimeter/zigzag/spiral bots only take detours that fit their natural movement pattern.
topics.decisions:
- **Shared scoring helper over bespoke per-bot logic**: A single reusable scoring function with configurable weights let every bot gain power-up awareness through one added line each, minimizing the risk of accidentally altering each bot's carefully tuned existing behavior.
- **Hard safety ceiling on pursuit bonus**: The power-up bonus is capped well below each bot's existing self-preservation thresholds, guaranteeing that no bot will ever choose a power-up over avoiding a fatal self-trap.
- **Distance- and lifetime-aware evaluation**: Bots discount or ignore power-ups that are unreachable or likely to disappear before they can arrive, so pursuit choices reflect realistic timing rather than chasing something that will vanish.

recap:
This work introduced a new collectible power-up system to the snake game, adding three effects: Double Points, Slow-Mo, and Shrink. Power-ups spawn occasionally after eating regular food, sit on the board for a limited time with a visible expiry blink, and can be triggered directly via a testing URL parameter. Collecting one shows a pop-up toast and, for the timed effects, a HUD badge with a countdown; Shrink applies instantly by trimming the snake's tail. The feature is available in single-player and bot-vs-bot modes, deliberately left out of human two-player matches to avoid confusion over whose pickup effect applies, and Slow-Mo affects the whole game's pace whenever either snake holds it in bot-vs-bot.

Alongside the player-facing feature, every one of the twelve automated bot opponents was updated to recognize and react to power-ups. Each bot got its own personality-appropriate appetite for pursuing pickups: aggressive bots chase Double Points and Slow-Mo hard, a tightly-coiling bot strongly favors Shrink to avoid trapping itself, cautious bots only pursue when it's safe, and bots with fixed movement patterns like sweeping, spiraling, or zigzagging only detour when a pickup naturally falls along their route. A safety limit ensures no bot will ever risk a self-trap just to grab a power-up, and pursuit decisions account for whether a pickup is reachable and likely to still be there by the time the bot arrives.
